title: Gael Monfils bids emotional farewell as Federer, Alcaraz, Nadal and Djokovic lead tributes to retired star
article_text:
Gael Monfils paid a touching tribute to his daughter Skai at the Paris Masters in his first public appearance since splitting from wife Elina Svitolina.

The tennis world was left stunned last month when Ukrainian Svitolina announced that after more than five years of marriage, her time with husband Monfils was coming to an end.

The world No 6 initially said the emotional scars of the Russia-Ukraine war were partly behind their separation, before later saying she was not entirely happy with the Frenchman.

Monfils hit out at the “venomous” abuse that had come the 32-year-old’s way, before admitting that he was struggling with the end of their relationship.

The 40-year-old quietly retired from tennis in early October, after taking himself off the anti-doping protocols, despite being scheduled to have his farewell at the Paris Masters. However, on Tuesday, he spoke in front of fans to bid an emotional goodbye.

The 13-time ATP Tour title winner said he was “happy” and “at peace” with his 22-year-long career, but did admit it has been “difficult saying goodbye”.

He said, “Thank you, Paris. I won’t hide that it’s difficult saying goodbye. The most beautiful thing that this earth has given me is you – the magnificent public, this Parisian public.

“I want to thank you. I’ve been a professional for 22 years. 22 years of an extraordinary story that I could not have dreamed of. If today I was able to achieve my dream, and it’s thanks to all of you.’

“I’m very proud of what I did. I was able to sit down – for a few hard weeks, I won’t hide it – but I was able to sit down and reflect on what I accomplished. I did the maximum, and I’m very happy and at peace with what I achieved.”

The former world No 6 also dedicated a big chunk of his speech to his four-year-old daughter Skai, whom he hopes can become a tennis “champion” one day. Monfils added that it is eight years to the day since he began a relationship with Svitolina, in a classy oration from the French legend.

In his speech, which has been translated by Tiempo De Tenis, “My little girl Skaï wanted me to talk about her because she told me: ‘You don’t talk about me enough, Daddy.’ And she’s only four years old! So Skaï, if you’re watching this, here I am talking about you. Maybe you’ll see it someday down the line.

“She asked me why people were coming up to say hi to me, and I told her it was because Daddy is very kind and she had to be kind too. She replied that she was going to be very kind as well. Then she told me she wanted to be a champion.

“I asked her what she wanted to be a champion in, and she said: ‘Everything.’ I told her she’d have to choose, and the first thing she blurted out was: ‘I want to be a champion of talking.’ Then she thought about it and told me she’d like to be a tennis champion, so she’s definitely got the right stuff for it.

“She wanted to dedicate this last match to her daddy. It was in Paris, on November 3, 2026. As an anecdote, today marks exactly 8 years since I was with your mom, so it’s a very symbolic date for the family.

“Skaï, your daddy was a tennis player, he loved tennis, he grew up in Paris and had an amazing crowd. I hope with all my heart that you become a champion in whatever you choose, and hopefully one day you can play here in Paris.”

Incidentally, after Ben Shelton beat Cameron Norrie in his opening match, he described Monfils as the “greatest entertainer in the history of tennis”.

And in a tribute video, the likes of Roger Federer, Rafael Nadal, Novak Djokovic, Carlos Alcaraz and more paid their respects to the Frenchman.

Djokovic said, “What an incredible career! One of the kindest and funniest guys. There’s no one who doesn’t like you, Gaël,” and Federer added, “We all wanted to be a little like Gaël Monfils. You have tons of fans.”

Alcaraz commented, “For me, you were a true inspiration and an exceptional athlete. The most important thing is that you’re a great person off the court,” while Nadal declared, “Congratulations on this formidable career. I remember the first time I saw you when we were just kids, and we made it! We had very long careers full of success.”

Jannik Sinner, Daniil Medvedev, and more also had kind words for Monfils, who is now preparing for a life in finance. While he is leaving tennis, he will not be forgotten.

WTA Finals Day 1 and 2 order of play: Rybakina to face Noskova in opener
article_text:
The groups are set, and now the opening schedule is, too. Following Tuesday’s draw for the 2026 WTA Finals, the Day 1 and Day 2 orders of play confirmed the first round-robin matchups in Indian Wells.

Here’s the schedule for both days, followed by a closer look at the singles matches.

- Noon PT: Elena Rybakina vs. Linda Noskova

- Followed by: Coco Gauff vs. Jessica Pegula

- Followed by: Katerina Siniakova/Taylor Townsend vs. Sara Errani/Jasmine Paolini

- Followed by: Cristina Bucsa/Nicole Melichar-Martinez vs. Ellen Perez/Demi Schuurs

A first meeting of 2026 between the last two major champions is set to open the WTA Finals. Rybakina brings both form -- riding a five-match winning streak -- and history, having never lost to Noskova. But the young Czech will be eager to make a statement in her debut at the year-end championships after winning her first Grand Slam title at Wimbledon earlier this year.

They pair last met in Wuhan in 2025, where Rybakina earned her third straight victory in the head-to-head, all in straight sets.

There is plenty of history between the friends and former doubles partners who have split their previous 10 meetings. The pair were drawn into the same group at last year's WTA Finals, where Dubai champion Pegula prevailed in three sets. But Cincinnati champion Gauff has won both of their 2026 encounters, in the Wimbledon quarterfinals and the Cincinnati final.

Overall, this marks the fourth consecutive year Gauff and Pegula have met at the year-end championships, with Pegula holding a 2-1 edge in their previous three matchups.

- Noon: Aryna Sabalenka vs. Karolina Muchova

- Followed by: Mirra Andreeva vs. Elina Svitolina

- Followed by: Gabriela Dabrowski/Luisa Stefani vs. Elise Mertens/ Zhang Shuai

- Followed by: Guo Hanyu /Kristina Mladenovic vs. Hsieh Su-wei /Jelena Ostapenko

Muchova holds a slight edge in the head-to-head through five meetings, though Sabalenka won their lone 2026 encounter in Brisbane in January. Sabalenka enjoyed several high points this season, winning the Brisbane title and completing the Sunshine Double, but losing the No. 1 ranking to Rybakina and falling to her in the Australian Open and US Open finals should provide plenty of motivation as she looks to replicate her Indian Wells success at the WTA Finals.

For Muchova, 2026 was a breakthrough campaign that earned her a first appearance at the WTA Finals. Highlights included her first title in seven years in Doha, another crown in Bad Homburg and a second Grand Slam final appearance at Wimbledon.

A classic youth-versus-experience matchup pits Andreeva against Svitolina, but despite the gap in age and experience, both enjoyed career-best seasons in 2026. Andreeva captured her first Grand Slam title at Roland Garros, while Svitolina captured titles in Auckland and Rome and reached another WTA 1000 final in Dubai.

The pair have met only twice, with Svitolina winning their only 2026 encounter at the Australian Open. Andreeva enters the year-end championships fresh off a runner-up finish in Beijing, while Svitolina reached back-to-back quarterfinals in Beijing and Wuhan.

TSN and RDS secure Canada Soccer rights for upcoming CONCACAF campaigns
article_text:
TSN and RDS, the Canadian sports networks owned by multimedia firm Bell Media, have secured exclusive rights to broadcast Canada Soccer’s national team games in upcoming competitions run by CONCACAF, North America’s soccer confederation.

The deal covers matches involving Canada’s men’s and women’s national teams in November and December, starting with the men’s two-legged CONCACAF Nations League quarter-final against Guatemala to be played at BMO Field in Toronto on November 16.

Combine business intelligence and editorial excellence to reach engaged professionals across 36 leading media platforms.

The aggregate winner will advance to the 2027 CONCACAF Nations League Finals in Los Angeles and secure qualification for the 2027 CONCACAF Gold Cup.

The women’s team, meanwhile, will begin their CONCACAF W Championship campaign against Panama on November 28, with the competition serving as a qualifier for both the FIFA Women’s World Cup Brazil 2027 and the Los Angeles 2028 Olympic Games.

TSN’s coverage of every Canada match will feature pre-game and half-time studio coverage. Both the men’s quarter-final series against Guatemala and the women’s W Championship matches will be aired in French on RDS.

The matches will also be shown via OneSoccer, the streaming platform owned by Canadian Soccer Media and Entertainment (CSME), the commercial arm of Canada Soccer.

Kevin Blue, Canada Soccer chief executive, said: “This window is a significant moment for both of our National Teams, with a place in the Concacaf Nations League Finals and qualification for the FIFA Women’s World Cup and the LA28 Olympic Games on the line.

“Canadians have shown how much these teams mean to them, and making these matches available across TSN, RDS and OneSoccer ensures fans across the country can follow them every step of the way.”

Canada Soccer is looking to build on record interest following the men’s FIFA World Cup 2026, which was co-hosted by the US, Canada, and Mexico earlier this year, as well as a recent international break which saw five national team friendlies aired across OneSoccer, TSN, and RDS in September and October.

CSME chief executive James Johnson said: “The growth of soccer in Canada is about more than any single tournament. It's about building sustained interest in the game and ensuring Canadians can follow their National Teams as they compete on the international stage.

“Concacaf competitions are a critical part of that journey, and we're pleased to work with TSN and RDS alongside OneSoccer to bring these important matches to audiences across the country.”

The broadcasts come as CSME, the rebranded commercial arm formerly known as Canada Soccer Business, continues to increase the visibility of the men’s and women’s national teams after securing a long-term partnership with Canada Soccer.

The agreement, struck in February, runs through 2037 and cemented a new revenue-sharing model that included a pledge to ensure wide broadcast distribution for Canadian national team games, with equitable coverage of both men’s and women’s teams.

In the past, revenue had not been shared. Instead, the former Canada Soccer Business paid Canada Soccer a set amount each year, around $3 million to $4 million, with the rest used by CSB to help fund the growing top-tier Canadian Premier League (CPL).

These new revenue-sharing terms are backstopped by a minimum annual sum that is guaranteed, and the agreement also comes with two additional lump-sum payments from CSME to Canada Soccer through the term.

Previously, the agreement covered both sponsorship revenue and media rights (relating to CSME’s OneSoccer OTT platform) and has now been expanded to include licensing and merchandising activity related to the Canada Soccer brand, expanding CSME’s remit.

During the partnership, there will be a “look-in period” every three years to ensure the terms remain tied to fair market value, and upon the expiry of the partnership, there will be a mutual option for a five-year extension.

Overseeing the collaboration will be a joint governance structure composed of executives from both bodies.

England handed Fin Smith injury boost with hope he can face Australia
article_text:

Fin Smith faces a pivotal practice session on Wednesday as England’s chief playmaker looks to prove his fitness for the autumn opener against Australia at Allianz Stadium.

Smith is to train alongside his international team-mates for the first time since injuring his calf in Northampton’s defeat by Leicester on 24 October.

England are increasingly optimistic the British and Irish Lion will prove he is ready for Sunday’s Nations Championship clash given he has so far progressed through every stage of his recovery.

Head coach Steve Borthwick names his team on Friday, potentially giving his first choice fly-half two full training sessions ahead of his hoped-for comeback in the first of four Tests this month.

If Smith fails to get the green light, Test centurion George Ford and Harlequins ringmaster Marcus Smith will compete for the number 10 jersey in a duel between experience and form.

“Fin is really good and he’s tracking nicely,” Smith’s Northampton team-mate Tommy Freeman said.

“He’s doing the right stuff with the physios. It’s always good having him there because of the connection I have with him at the club, which will always be beneficial for me.”

Whoever features against Australia, they will partner Jack van Poortvliet at half-back as England reel from the loss of Alex Mitchell for the entire campaign.

A scan has revealed Mitchell’s fourth hamstring issue of 2026 – a grim succession of injuries affecting both legs – requires weeks of rehabilitation, ruling him out of the Tests against Australia, Japan and New Zealand as well as finals weekend.

It occurred when playing for Northampton against Gloucester on Saturday and with another Saints scrum-half, Archie McParland, out for at least the Australia game because of a calf issue, England have been forced to add Ben Spencer and Harry Randall to their squad.

“To see Mitch go off like that is not nice, but these things happen,” Freeman said. “It’s sport, it comes with the game. We’re gutted for Mitch and hopefully it’s a good recovery for him.”

Freeman’s own place in the team appears to be on the wing having started there for the last two Tests, wins against Fiji and Argentina during the first phase of the Nations Championship in July.

The Lions star began the tour at outside centre in the clash with South Africa – his sixth consecutive Test start in the midfield – but England appear to have shelved experimenting with his position, at least for now.

“The wing’s been a bit of a focus,” Freeman said. “Playing there and having that continuity there is probably where I’m very comfortable.

“But I’ll always have the ability to go into midfield if needs be. You see across a number of teams there are players who have the ability to cover positions.

“My point of difference is when I get my hands on the ball and create a threat. That’s when I can get some go-forward and put other boys into good positions.”

title: Death threats for Briton Burrage on WTA Tour return
article_text:
Britain's Jodie Burrage received death threats and abuse on social media after she was beaten in her first WTA Tour singles match proper for 16 months.

The 27-year-old, ranked 474th in the world, suffered a first-round exit at the Chennai Open after India's Vaishnavi Adkar fought back from a set down to triumph 3-6 6-3 7-5.

Burrage later shared a story on her Instagram account, external with a video scroll of direct messages, including abuse, she was sent following the match.

"Nice welcome back to tour. I remember why I left," said the Londoner in the accompanying message.

Germany's Eva Lys showed solidarity with Burrage, tagging the WTA from her Instagram handle and asking: "When will something be done?"

British number 15 Burrage's last match on the WTA Tour, excluding qualifiers, was in July 2025 when she lost to Catherine McNally in the first round at Wimbledon.

Female tennis players were subjected to more than 12,000 abusive posts and messages on social media last year, according to a report published earlier this year.

Data from the Signify Group's threat matrix service, which uses artificial intelligence-led detection, showed a similar number of abusive posts in 2025 to 2024.

A report from the same group two years ago found that angry gamblers were behind 48% of posts which were deemed to be abusive.

They were responsible for 42% of verified abuse in 2025 and 59% of cases of serious abuse.

In 2025, Britain's Katie Boulter told BBC Sport she had received death threats.

Fellow players called for identity verification to be introduced by social media platforms to try to address the issue.

The WTA's player board has previously condemned the abuse as "unacceptable" and said the impact can be "significant".

title: Novak Djokovic: Seven-time Rolex Paris Masters champion keeps chances of making ATP Finals in Turin alive
article_text:
Novak Djokovic maintained his Nitto ATP Finals qualification hopes at the Rolex Paris Masters, where he rallied from a set and a break down to defeat Valentin Vacherot.

The seven-time Paris champion was pushed hard by the Monegasque and overcame a mid-match shoulder issue to defeat the Basel champion 6-7 (5-7) 7-5 6-1.

Djokovic requires at least a semi-final run in Paris to give himself a chance of qualifying for the season-ending ATP Finals in Turin.

Djokovic is 11th in the Race To Turin on 2,940 points but must finish inside the top nine to qualify. Rafael Jodar, still alive in Paris, is currently ninth on 3,234 points, 294 points clear of Djokovic.

Asked on Sky Sports how he was feeling physically, Djokovic, who next plays Australian Rinky Hijikata, said: "Not the freshest but obviously glad to turn this match around.

"A lot of players tell me it's completely different conditions to what it was last year.

"It's very slow and bouncy this year, just super, super quick, and Vacherot won his tournament title in Basel a few days ago, super confident and you could feel that in his game, particularly off that first serve. Not too many double faults, he's going for his second serve as well.

"His third serve is quicker than my first so it's very difficult to face someone like that. I should have taken that first set, just an awful volley at 5-4 and next thing you know you're down a set and down a break."

"I'm glad that I kind of found a way to turn this match around."

"Djokovic is so used to being seeded high and at least get himself into the draw without having to suffer through that first round. This is a physical match, and if he wants to go deep in the tournament, especially here in Paris because this is a shorter Masters tournament 1000. This isn't one of those Masters tournaments where you have a day off between every match, so this is going to be a little tricker for him."

British No 1 Arthur Fery may have hit a career-high world No 32 and produced the shot of the match with a between-the-legs drop-shot winner, but he was ultimately taken out by home favourite Quentin Halys 7-6 (8-6) 7-5.

Fery was unable to take two set points in the first-set tie-break with big-serving Frenchman Halys claiming the only break of serve in the second for victory.

British No 2 Cameron Norrie also made an early exit, as he was swept aside 6-3 6-4 by US Open finalist Ben Shelton.

Shelton, who has captured four tour-level titles, including his second ATP Masters 1000 crown in Canada and reached a maiden Grand Slam final at the US Open this year, announced that he will add Alcaraz's former mentor Juan Carlos Ferrero to his team in 2027.

"Juan Carlos is one of the great minds in tennis," Shelton said.

"His experience of winning at the highest level and developing champions will be a huge asset to our team."

Ferrero said: "Ben has extraordinary talent, power and character. I'm looking forward to contributing my experience and working together with everyone to help Ben achieve his ambitions."

Taylor Fritz rallied from a set down to defeat French qualifier Benjamin Bonzi 3-6 6-3 6-4 to reach the second round where he faces another qualifier, Alex Molcan.

Tommy Paul, currently 13th in the Race To Turin on 2,775 points, beat Holger Rune 7-5 6-4.

Flavio Cobolli has announced his withdrawal from the Masters 1000 event on social media.

"I was really hoping I could make it," Cobolli wrote in his Instagram Stories. "Today, after media day, I tried training in the gym, but I'm still feeling some discomfort and I don't want to take any risks. So I've decided to withdraw from Paris.

"This one really hurts. This city gave me the two biggest weeks of my career this year, and playing here again would have meant a lot. Now it's all about recovering. Thank you for always being there."

Despite his withdrawal from the ATP Masters 1000 event in Paris, Cobolli remains in contention to make his Nitto ATP Finals debut.

The Italian is currently sixth in the Race To Turin, 466 points ahead of ninth-placed Rafael Jodar, who is effectively in the final qualification spot.

Britain's Jodie Burrage suffered a first-round loss in a gruelling encounter at the Chennai Open on Tuesday.

Taking on local wild card Vaishnavi Adkar, Britain's Burrage looked poised for victory when she led 5-3 in the deciding set but she lost four games in a row to fall to a 3-6 6-3 7-5 defeat after two hours and 47 minutes.

Burrage, who has not won a tour-level match since Eastbourne last summer, appeared to struggle with the humid conditions and called the doctor with her opponent about to serve for the match.

Burrage was visibly shaking and had her blood pressure and oxygen levels checked as well as ice rubbed on her arms and legs. She was able to resume the contest but lost the final game to love.

title: Dakar Olympics: Rising Lionesses book place in rugby sevens final against Australia
article_text:
Rising Lionesses have booked their place in the rugby sevens final at the Dakar 2026 Youth Olympic Games, setting up another showdown with Australia, while the country’s swimmers endured a difficult second day in the pool.

The Rising Lionesses continued their impressive run in Dakar, Senegal, despite suffering a 19-5 defeat to Australia in their final group-stage encounter. The result, however, did little to derail their campaign as they progressed to the semifinals, where they faced Madagascar.

The Kenyan youngsters responded emphatically, overcoming the Malagasy side 15-5 to secure their place in the final and keep their gold medal hopes alive.

They will now renew their rivalry with Australia in the final, scheduled for 8:03 pm, in what promises to be an exciting contest.

Having already met in the group stage, the Rising Lionesses will be keen to turn the tables and finish their campaign on the highest possible note.

Meanwhile, it was a challenging day for Kenya’s swimmers, with all three athletes who competed failing to advance to the finals in their respective events.

Jeremy Rieck was the first Kenyan in action in the men's 100 metres backstroke. Competing in Heat Four, he clocked 59.15 seconds but fell short of securing a place in the final.

Macrine Kolombo followed in the women's 100 metres breaststroke, recording 1:23.33 in Heat Two, while Neo Olengo clocked 1:08.49 in Heat Three of the men's 100 metres breaststroke. Both swimmers also failed to progress.

Despite the setbacks, the Kenyan swimmers will have other opportunities to make their mark as the competition continues.

Kolombo will return to the pool for the women's 200 meters individual medley before concluding her campaign on Thursday, 5 November, in the 50 meters breaststroke.

Olengo's next assignment will be the men's 50 meters freestyle before he wraps up his tourney on Thursday, 5 November, in the 50 meters breaststroke.

Rieck, who reached the men's 100 meters butterfly final on the opening day, will compete in the 50 meters butterfly before closing his campaign in the 50 meters backstroke on Thursday, 5 November.

Isabelle Mwangi is yet to make her debut at the Games. She will begin her campaign in the women's 50 meters freestyle before concluding with the 200 meters freestyle on Friday, 6 November.

title: ‘I don’t feel there’s any risk’: Rory McIlroy confident in UAE safety ahead of Abu Dhabi Championship
article_text:
Dubai: Rory McIlroy has insisted he feels completely safe competing in the UAE despite ongoing uncertainty across the wider Middle East, as the Northern Irish golfer prepares for this week's Abu Dhabi HSBC Championship.

Speaking to the media ahead of the tournament, which takes place at Yas Links from November 5-8, McIlroy addressed concerns surrounding travel to the region and explained why he remains confident about competing in the Emirates.

"Even if something was to happen, I wouldn't feel unsafe."

The four-time Major champion also praised the UAE's security capabilities, suggesting he would remain comfortable in the country even if the regional situation were to change.

"The UAE has great defensive systems," he said.

"If they closed the airspace like they did before I would still feel safe, I wouldn't feel like I'd be in any danger."

"I kept asking the questions to the DP World Tour and everyone deems that it's safe to be here, so who am I to say otherwise."

His comments come as the UAE prepares to host two of the biggest tournaments on the DP World Tour calendar, with the Abu Dhabi HSBC Championship followed by the season-ending DP World Tour Championship at Jumeirah Golf Estates in Dubai.

Both events form part of the DP World Tour Play-Offs, where the leading players compete for valuable ranking points and the opportunity to finish the season as Race to Dubai champion.

For McIlroy, the decision to compete in the UAE is also driven by his determination to finish the year strongly and make history, with the Northern Irishman chasing an eighth Race to Dubai title that would see him equal Colin Montgomerie's all-time record, while also securing a fifth consecutive crown.

"This is important to me, I want to end my year well and have a chance to win another Race to Dubai," he said.

"I don't feel like there's any risk coming here but if I didn't feel like there was a risk, the reward is worth it."

title: SVNS Series great Portia Woodman-Wickliffe takes on coaching role
article_text:
Black Ferns Sevens great Portia Woodman-Wickliffe has been announced as one of two Bolt Women coaches ahead of Ignite7 in Tauranga this weekend, overseeing a squad that includes a couple of HSBC SVNS Series players.

Woodman-Wickliffe retired from international sevens after New Zealand’s successful quest for gold at the Paris Olympics, hanging up the boots as a two-time gold medallist and a dual Rugby World Cup winner in 15s.

The New Zealander is still the all-time top try-scorer on the women’s SVNS Series, has won gold medals at the Rugby World Cup Sevens and Commonwealth Games, and was recognised in 2020 as the World Rugby Women’s Sevens Player of the Decade.

Woodman-Wickliffe has been unveiled as a Bolt Women coach along with Hare Makiri, ahead of the event on November 7 to 8 at Tauranga’s Blake Park. Danii Mafoe and Maia Davis bring Black Ferns Sevens experience into the roster.

Ella Henderson has also been named, just a few days after representing the inaugural New Zealand Under-21s side against Australia NextGen U21. Henderson started at inside centre and took on vice-captaincy duties.

Kaia Walker-Waitoa, Keira Su’a-Smith Lita Bulicakau, Phoebe Edwards, Sariyah Paitai, Shyrah Tuliau-Tua’a, Sienna Stowers-Smith, Tianne Tavita Fesolai and Winnie Palamo round out the Bolt Women squad.

Matt Howling and Solomona Paraki will oversee the men’s side, which includes a player slot that is still to be filled. David Kama, Gavin Holder, Harry Carter, Jacob McKinnon, Kees Kolose, Konelio Burgess, Louis Lepionika, Reimana Saunderson-Rurawhe, Suli Pahulu, Tametai Wihongi and Taniela Maisiri make up Bolt Men.

Former All Blacks Sevens playmakers Kurt Baker and Gillies Kaka will take on coaching roles with Surge Men and Inferno Men, respectively. Two-time Olympic gold medallist Theresa Setefano is another big-name taking on coaching responsibilities.

Sindhu raises red flag over badminton's 25-second rule
article_text:
Two-time Olympic medallist PV Sindhu, chair of the BWF Athletes' Commission, is advocating for a review of the Badminton World Federation's controversial 25-second shot clock rule, citing widespread player concerns and recent on-court incidents.

- PV Sindhu, as BWF Athletes' Commission chair, has conveyed player concerns about the 25-second shot clock rule to the Badminton World Federation.

- The shot clock, currently being trialled, requires players to be ready to serve within 25 seconds after a rally, leading to yellow and red cards.

- Players and umpires initially found it challenging to adapt, with ongoing debates about its fairness, particularly after a controversial red card incident at the French Open.

- Sindhu expects the BWF to review the shot clock system soon, acknowledging that while athletes are adapting, some aspects need reconsideration for fairness.

- The introduction of the 15-point scoring system in the future could further impact the dynamics of the game in relation to the shot clock.

Two-time Olympic-medallist P V Sindhu on Wednesday said she expects the Badminton World Federation's 25-second shot clock innovation to undergo a review after multiple concerns were conveyed to the world body about its fairness by her and several other players.

The shot clock is being trialled at select BWF World Tour tournaments this year. Under the regulation, players have 25 seconds after the end of a rally to be ready to serve.

"There have been a lot of ups and downs. For some people, it's still new, and sometimes a few umpires are very strict. There are instances of yellow cards and red cards...," Sindhu said in a virtual interaction on Wednesday.

"We've been getting used to the 25-second clock. It's been almost seven tournaments now, and there's been a lot of improvement. Initially, it was really hard for both the umpires and the players to understand because sometimes the receiver would be ready, but the server wouldn't be, and sometimes it would be the other way around," she explained.

"It took some time to understand how this 25-second clock works. Sometimes there are still five or seven seconds left, but the umpire says 'your opponent is ready, so why aren't you?'...but there is still seven seconds. There's been a lot of discussion on this."

Sindhu, who is also the chairperson of the BWF Athletes' Commission, said she has conveyed the players' concerns to the governing body and that the system is expected to undergo a review.

"Being the chair of the Athletes' Commission in the BWF, I've notified and I have given my thoughts. Players had come to me and told me what they feel. I've seen a lot of change in terms of how umpires are making sure it is getting used the right way. And there's been a lot of changes and umpires also have been understanding," she said.

"When you go through a long rally, everybody needs to understand that we are human beings. For players also, it's really hard. So there needs to be some understanding.

"At the same time, as athletes, we also understand that we need to be prepared earlier and know what is expected of us. We are getting used to it, and we know that there can be warnings if we are not ready."

On the debate over warnings and penalties, Sindhu said: "There's been a lot of debate as well in terms of a couple of players are like, 'but how is this fair that we are coming on time but still the umpires are giving a warning'. So, there are some debates on this. I've given my points."

At the French Open, home favourites Thom Gicquel and Delphine Delrue, also the reigning world champions, were hit with a highly unusual red card penalty at 19-19 in the deciding game against China's world No. 1 pair, Feng Yan Zhe and Huang Dong Ping.

It resulted in an automatic point awarded to Feng and Huang, who converted the subsequent rally to win the match 21-19 and advance to the final.

The direct intervention of the automated time clock at such a critical juncture sparked widespread criticism from players and fans over the rigidity of the trial rule.

"I've seen what happened in the French Open semi-finals, and I've put my thoughts in. They're going through it and they're going to review it soon and come back. But couple of people are okay with it, couple of people are getting used to it but couple of them are still taking time to understand it.

"But I'm sure that it will definitely change and everybody will come into a conclusion. But at the same time, sometimes it's sad for one person, one athlete, one player. sometimes unknowingly after a wrong rally, unknowingly, let's say you're tired or it's tactic or taking a break or not coming on time. Unknowingly, umpires might show you a red card or yellow card.

title: Indian cricket scores big as automotive giants ramp up sponsorship spending to US$123 million
article_text:
Indian cricket has emerged as the biggest force in Asia-Pacific automotive sports sponsorship, attracting US$122.9 million in 2025 and accounting for 34.2 per cent of the region’s total sponsorship value, according to new GlobalData research.

The Asia-Pacific automotive sports sponsorship market reached a record US$359.5 million in 2025, with cricket contributing more than two-thirds of the sector’s growth since 2020.

GlobalData’s report, Sponsorship Sector Report – Automotive – APAC 2026, found that automotive sponsorship spending on cricket increased by 64.7 per cent over the five-year period, making it one of the few sports in the region to record annual value growth since 2020.

The Indian Premier League (IPL) and the Board of Control for Cricket in India (BCCI) have attracted premium sponsorship deals by offering automotive brands access to large national audiences and strong connections with cricket fans.

Olivia Snooks, Sport Analyst at GlobalData, said automotive brands were increasingly partnering with cricket properties across the Asia-Pacific region, particularly in India.

“India cricket accounted for three of the top 10 largest automotive deals across the region in 2025, including Tata Motors’ IPL title sponsorship deal, which is the largest across APAC.”

The report found that 46.3 per cent of the region’s automotive sponsorship deal value in 2025 came from just 11 agreements worth US$5 million or more.

The number of active automotive brands sponsoring sports across Asia-Pacific also increased significantly, from 117 in 2020 to 274 in 2025.

During 2025, 69 brands entered the region’s automotive sponsorship market for the first time, signing 71 deals. More than half of the new entrants were Japanese brands, accounting for 36 deals, while Chinese brands accounted for 10.

Many of the new partnerships were smaller brand-awareness campaigns linked to major team sports, including the IPL, Australia’s National Rugby League (NRL) and Australian Football League (AFL). Others involved motorsport competitions such as Asian Le Mans and Supercars, as well as baseball and Olympic-related partnerships.

However, 62 brands that had active sponsorship agreements in 2024 exited the market in 2025, withdrawing more than twice the financial value brought in by new entrants.

Snooks said the exit was led by Roewe’s US$8 million departure, which was directly offset by the entry of its parent company, SAIC Motor.

The report also highlighted contrasting strategies among major automotive sponsors. Tata Motors committed US$64.3 million across three high-value deals, while Toyota spent US$33.4 million across 11 mid-sized partnerships.

Tata Motors and Apollo Tyres concentrated their investments on major cricket sponsorships, while companies such as Toyota and BKT pursued a broader strategy through multiple partnerships. Tyre manufacturers accounted for four of the region’s top 12 sponsorship positions.

Over five years, automotive sponsorship spending increased at an average annual rate of 10.5 per cent across the sector, but individual brands followed different trajectories.

Apollo Tyres recorded growth of 67.4 per cent, Tata Motors 52.6 per cent and Nissan 36.4 per cent, while Hyundai reduced its spending by 17.2 per cent, Hero MotoCorp by 14.3 per cent and Yamaha by 12.2 per cent.

GlobalData said only seven automotive brands maintained continuous year-on-year sponsorship growth from 2020.

The findings underline the growing commercial influence of Indian cricket in the Asia-Pacific sports sponsorship market, with the IPL and BCCI attracting major investments from automotive companies seeking large audiences and national brand visibility.

title: Clark Laidlaw 'open to conversation' over becoming next Scotland coach
article_text:
Clark Laidlaw has insisted his focus remains firmly on the Hurricanes despite being linked with a potential future return to Scotland.

Laidlaw was asked whether he would welcome discussions with Scottish Rugby should the national coaching position become available after next year's Rugby World Cup, after which it is widely expected Gregor Townsend will end his decade in charge of Scotland.

While flattered by the suggestion, Laidlaw - the cousin of former Scotland captain Greig and son of 1984 Grand Slam hero Roy - was reluctant to look too far ahead, though did admit he would be open to having conversations with Scottish Rugby.

“I would welcome a conversation. I’m not sure where that would get to,” he told BBC Sport Scotland.

"Family-wise, it would be a big thing to u sticks and move back to Scotland. But yeah, you never know in in sport. One thing I have learned, you can't plan too much. Opportunities will come. Sometimes you are least expecting them, good and bad. That's the reality of professional sport.

"My focus at the minute will be to prepare the Hurricanes as best possible and to try and continue to improve as a coach and a leader in this club.

"If that leads to international rugby eventually somewhere one day, that will be something that I would definitely look at but. But I've definitely learned that looking too far ahead in sport can can trip you up."

Laidlaw was quick to praise the work being carried out at Murrayfield, highlighting the progress made under Gregor Townsend and the wider coaching structure across the professional game.

“I’ve really enjoyed watching Scotland the last few years,” he said.

“Gregor [Townsend] and the team there have done an amazing job, not only with the top team but through the pro teams as well.”

He singled out Glasgow Warriors coach Franco Smith for particular praise and also noted Edinburgh Rugby’s improved start to the season under a strengthened coaching group.

title: Rafael Nadal: Tennis legend set to join Real Madrid board of directors
article_text:
Tennis great Rafael Nadal is set to join the board of Spanish football giants Real Madrid.

Nadal won 22 Grand Slam titles, two Olympic gold medals and helped Spain claim five Davis Cups before retiring in 2024.

Real's members will be asked to approve the 40-year-old's appointment to the board at a meeting later this month.

In a statement announcing the move, external, the club said Nadal was "one of the greatest legends in the history of sport and one of the most admired and recognised Spanish athletes in the world".

"It is a great source of pride that a figure of his sporting and human stature, a benchmark of Spanish and world sport, will become part of our board of directors and contribute, from this position of responsibility, to the present and future of our club," Real added.

The tennis legend - a boyhood Real fan who holds member's number 67,778 - included a photo of himself as a child in a club kit in his response to the news.

"I want to thank president Florentino Perez and the board for proposing that I join the board of directors of Real Madrid," Nadal said in his post on X, external.

"I have accepted this proposal with great excitement, a desire to learn, and a willingness to contribute everything I can."

It is currently unclear as to what responsibilities Nadal would hold on the club's board.

Perez was re-elected to serve a new four-year term as Real president in June, having held the office since 2009.

He swiftly appointed Jose Mourinho to a second spell as head coach, hoping to improve the club's fortunes after they went a second season without a trophy in La Liga, the Champions League or the Copa del Rey.

Real are currently third in the league after 11 games - three points behind defending champions Barcelona.

title: Jodie Burrage: British tennis player receives death threats and social media abuse after defeat
article_text:
Britain's Jodie Burrage received death threats and abuse on social media after she was beaten in her first WTA Tour singles match proper for 16 months.

The 27-year-old, ranked 474th in the world, suffered a first-round exit at the Chennai Open after India's Vaishnavi Adkar fought back from a set down to triumph 3-6 6-3 7-5.

Burrage later shared a story on her Instagram account, external with a video scroll of direct messages, including abuse, she was sent following the match.

"Nice welcome back to tour. I remember why I left," said the Londoner in the accompanying message.

Germany's Eva Lys showed solidarity with Burrage, tagging the WTA from her Instagram handle and asking: "When will something be done?"

British number 15 Burrage's last match on the WTA Tour, excluding qualifiers, was in July 2025 when she lost to Catherine McNally in the first round at Wimbledon.

Female tennis players were subjected to more than 12,000 abusive posts and messages on social media last year, according to a report published earlier this year.

Data from the Signify Group's threat matrix service, which uses artificial intelligence-led detection, showed a similar number of abusive posts in 2025 to 2024.

A report from the same group two years ago found that angry gamblers were behind 48% of posts which were deemed to be abusive.

They were responsible for 42% of verified abuse in 2025 and 59% of cases of serious abuse.

In 2025, Britain's Katie Boulter told BBC Sport she had received death threats.

Fellow players called for identity verification to be introduced by social media platforms to try to address the issue.

The WTA's player board has previously condemned the abuse as "unacceptable" and said the impact can be "significant".

title: WTA and TikTok Form a Global Content Partnership
article_text:
Earlier this week, the Women’s Tennis Association (WTA) and global social media platform TikTok announced a special partnership that builds on an existing relationship between the two organizations. The partnership will involve several upcoming WTA tournaments, including the 2026 WTA Finals.

On November 2nd, the WTA and TikTok announced a global content partnership that intends to expand how fans discover and experience women’s tennis. The collaboration will focus on a mix of “player-led storytelling, creator content, and innovative digital experiences” at events on the WTA Tour.

The partnership’s first digital event was TikTok exclusively streaming the official Draw Ceremony for the 2026 WTA Finals on November 3rd. The social media company will host other livestreams in the future, and they will establish a dedicated sports content experience called TikTok GamePlan at various eligible WTA 1000 events, select WTA 500 tournaments, and this year’s WTA Finals in Indian Wells.

As part of the partnership, the WTA and TikTok are going to work with some of the top women’s tennis players to build their presence on the social media platform. According to the WTA press release, all TikTok posts with the #WTA hashtag have seen a 50% increase in views over the past calendar year.

TikTok’s Global Head of Sport Rolllo Goldstaub said in the same press release that “the passionate and growing women's tennis and sports community on TikTok helps fans discover athletes, celebrate big moments and bring their own perspectives to the game.”

“Together with the WTA, we’re giving sports fans more ways to experience the Tour,” he continued. “From player-led storytelling and creator access to live moments and dedicated destinations with TikTok GamePlan. It’s about making the Tour part of the conversation on TikTok and giving new audiences and tennis lovers an even closer connection to the players and moments they can discover on TikTok.”

The official partnership between the WTA and TikTok is part of a growing trend of tennis content creation on various social media platforms. The presence and behavior of content creators at the 2026 US Open caused much online discourse, and the All England Tennis Club announced shortly after that content creators would not receive formal credentials at Wimbledon 2027.

Despite this mixed reception by tennis fans and organizers, the collaboration between the WTA and TikTok will further support digital creators and their presence at official events. The WTA Creator Club will be a formal initiative that gives content creators special access to WTA tournaments and “unique content opportunities” designed by both organizations.

The official WTA press release ended with Sarah Swanson, WTA’s Chief Brand Officer, saying, "Women's tennis is having a real cultural moment, and our players are at the heart of it. They're not only extraordinary athletes, but global personalities who are influencing conversations far beyond sport.”

“Our work with TikTok over the past year has demonstrated the growing global momentum behind women's tennis and the potential to reach and engage audiences in new ways,” she continued. “By combining the power of our players and tournaments with TikTok's creativity and reach, we’re looking forward to making women's tennis more accessible and engaging for the next generation."

Zach Humphrey is a Senior Content Analyst at Point Curve with more than a decade of experience in publishing, marketing, sports writing, and digital content. He has written and edited thousands of pieces of content, with a focus on quality journalism. Zach co-created Tennis Library and has also written for Pickleball Squid. He holds a master’s degree in English and American Literature from NYU and grew up in an avid tennis family - his grandfather, Harry Kenney, was a tennis pro. Outside of work, Zach enjoys reading at New York City coffee shops, watching just about any sport played on ice, and going out for hot pot with friends.

title: Hampstead’s Dart crazy WTA Tour single title win at 2026 Guangzhou Open
article_text:
Hampstead tennis ace Harriet Dart celebrated her crazy week at 2026 Guangzhou Open claiming her first WTA Tour singles title, writes Ziad Chaudry.

The 30-year-old defeated Austria’s up-and-coming teenage sensation Lilli Tagger, ranked number 53 on the WTA Tour Driven by Mercedes-Benz world rankings, 4-6, 6-3, 6-4 in two hours and 18 minutes on the hardcourts of Nansha International Tennis Centre, Guangzhou, China to scoop the $37,390 (£27,700) winners’ cheque along with lifting the plate-type trophy.

Dart’s journey to being champion in this WTA250-ranked event began in the first qualifying round beating Hong Kong’s Cheuk Ying Shek 5-7, 7-6(5), 6-1. After easily disposing Mei Yamaguchi from Japan 6-2, 6-1 in the final qualifying round, the GB Billie Jean King Cup regular disposed Russia’s Tatiana Prozorova (6-4, 2-6, 6-2), world-ranked 46 Janice Tjen of Indonesia (6-4, 3-6, 6-3), Spain’s former world number two Paula Badosa (3-6, 6-2, 6-4) and Chinese home favourite Sun Xinran (5-7, 7-6(1), 6-0) before defeating Tagger, the 2025 Roland Garros junior girls singles champion Tagger and this year’s Livesport Prague Open WTA 250 event winner, in the final.

During the summer months Dart won two WTA Tour doubles titles alongside Glasgow-based Maia Lumsden also at WTA 250 level. The Lexus Nottingham Open during the pre-Wimbledon build up in June was later followed by Livesport Prague Open.

“It’s been years and years of playing since I was a little girl and it was something I’ve dreamt of being able to lift a trophy on the WTA Tour,” Dart told BBC Sport. “To be able to finally do it, I think many people counted me out many times.

"It's a bit crazy to be honest to sitting here as champion after coming through qualifying - it's mad really.

"It's been an incredible week for me and I'm super proud of myself. To be able to come through a week like this and leave here as champion is pretty cool and something new for me.”

This success in the Southern Chinese city has seen Dart return into the WTA Tour’s world top 100 rankings for the first time since November 2024 to number 84. She will also go straight into the main women’s singles draw of next year’s Grand Slam-season opener Australian Open in January.

title: Premier Jumping League unveils Fever as ticketing partner
article_text:
The Premier Jumping League (PJL), the new global show jumping competition launching next year, has named ticketing and entertainment tech provider Fever as an official partner as it prepares for its inaugural season.

The tie-up will see Fever use its demand-generation technology and global distribution network across the PJL’s nine-event calendar, staged across North America, Europe, and the Middle East, as it looks to boost audience reach.

Combine business intelligence and editorial excellence to reach engaged professionals across 36 leading media platforms.

Fever’s general manager Hannah Joos commented: “The PJL is bringing show jumping to an extended fan base, building a sustainable future for the sport and putting the fan experience at its center.

“That's exactly where Fever can help: our platform connects the league with new audiences, our ticketing and premium offers strengthen its commercial foundation, and our data-driven approach makes every event day more personal.”

The partnership with Fever forms the backbone of the PJL’s plans to make elite showjumping more accessible and bring the sport to new audiences around the world, which will sit alongside the league’s free-to-air broadcast strategy and a production partnership with Box-to-Box Films, the production company behind the popular Formula 1 documentary ‘Drive to Survive.’

Neil Moffitt, chief executive of the PJL, added: “Fever brings proven technology, global reach and a deep understanding of how to identify and engage audiences beyond traditional fanbases.

“This partnership gives us the infrastructure to turn that reach into attendance across our global calendar, introducing more people to the extraordinary athletes and competition at the heart of our sport.

“As we build towards our first season in 2027, Fever will be an important partner in delivering our ambition to make elite showjumping more accessible to audiences around the world.”

Last week, the PJL announced the appointment of Aurora Media Worldwide as its host broadcast production partner under a three-year agreement.

Under the deal, Aurora will lead the production of the PJL's international host broadcast feed, highlights programming, and behind-the-scenes coverage across all nine events, which will make FTA part of its strategy to increase reach.

The broadcast agreement came five months after the league issued a tender for a host broadcast partner in May, two months after the league announced it would launch with a guaranteed prize pot of $300 million.

Most recently, horseracing’s governing body, the FEI, formally approved the league’s competition format, team structure and prize money distribution.

Starting in April 2027, the PJL will feature 16 teams competing across 14 international venues, with the competition aiming to create a sustainable economic model via a centralized sponsorship and broadcasting model. The events will involve top riders, including world number one Scott Brash.

The league is backed by McCourt Global, the investment firm of American billionaire and prolific sports team owner Frank McCourt, who previously held a 50% stake in the premium show jumping series, the Global Champions Tour, and founded the show jumping team, the Miami Celtics.

McCourt, who is named as founder and chairman of PJL, currently owns French soccer club Olympique de Marseille, but previously owned baseball’s iconic Los Angeles Dodgers.

To help attract new audiences, the league has partnered with production company Box to Box Films, the producers of the popular Formula 1 motor racing series 'Drive to Survive'.

The $300 million on offer across the nine events is one of the biggest investments in an equestrian competition.

By comparison, show jumping’s top-tier Global Tour distributed €22 million across its final flagship events last year, the Global Champions Tour and Global Champions League finals in Riyadh, as well as the Global Champions Prague Playoffs.

Specifically, €10.5 million was distributed across the 2025 LGCT and GCL Season Championships in Riyadh, which featured the world’s best athletes, while the GC Prague Playoffs saw a prize fund of more than €11.4 million split between the GCL Super Cup (€10 million) and GC Tour Super Grand Prix (€1.25 million).

title: Back in control: How Hyrox plans to make hybrid racing a TV and Olympic spectacle
article_text:
Back in September, Hyrox co-founder Moritz Fürste had a clear message for the company’s community of fitness racers: “You’re not getting rid of us anytime soon.”

Reports that Swiss agency Infront Sports & Media planned to sell its majority holding in Hyrox had led to speculation that Fürste and his co-founder Christian Toetzke might also be exiting the business. But in an Instagram video fittingly filmed in a gym, the pair were all smiles as they announced that they weren’t going anywhere.

Instead, Fürste and Toetzke confirmed that they were partnering with a consortium led by consumer-focused private equity firm L Catterton to take back control of Hyrox in a deal reportedly valuing the nine-year-old company at €600 million (US$700 million).

Infront initially invested in the fitness phenomenon in 2019 before taking a majority shareholding in 2022, though the deal stipulated that the Hyrox team would retain most of the direction and control over commercial decisions.

Even so, Fürste describes regaining a controlling stake as a “super important step”.

“I think opportunities arise at times,” he says, reflecting on the deal during an interview at the SportAccord Forum in Lausanne. “And there was the opportunity to get back into the majority shareholding of Hyrox, which we always wanted.

“We did not necessarily want to sell in 2022. There were different circumstances that led to the fact that it happened. But we always said that we would like to regain majority.

“We were calling the shots to the most extent before, and we also have had a good relationship with our former investor Infront Sports & Media. But of course, being in the driver’s seat officially is also an important aspect for founders.”

Announcing the deal at the time, Fürste said the fresh investment represented a “pivotal next step in the rapid evolution of the Hyrox success story”.

According to the announcement, Hyrox hopes to benefit from LVMH-backed L Catterton’s ‘extensive experience scaling high-growth consumer and fitness businesses’ like sandal maker Birkenstock, connected fitness specialist Peloton and French fashion label APC – names that suggest the private equity firm views Hyrox as much a lifestyle brand as a fitness race.

Indeed, since launching in 2017, Hyrox has earned a reputation as one of the world’s fastest-growing mass participation sports and has built a loyal following of fitness fanatics who travel the globe to take part. Typically held inside large convention centres or arenas, its races comprise eight lung-busting 1km runs, each followed by a functional workout such as sled pulls, burpee broad jumps or sandbag lunges.

Built to give everyday gym goers something to train for, Hyrox expects to host roughly 2.5 million participants and 2.89 million spectators at around 135 events across its 2026/27 season, according to Fürste.

With more than 600 employees spread across offices in Germany, the UK and US, the company has scaled rapidly and hosts races in more than 35 countries globally, many of which take place simultaneously on different continents during the same weekend, including in markets like Australia, Brazil, China, France, India and Japan.

That trajectory offers a sample of why Hyrox attracted new investors. Yet its breathless growth has been difficult to keep pace with – sometimes even for the organisation itself. Fürste admits it has been “super intense” and says the immediate priority is not so much moving into new markets, but rather building the internal structures required to sustain the company’s expansion and ensure the same quality across all of its events.

There is also plenty that Hyrox’s new investors should bring to the table, and Fürste says their involvement will be “strategic to some extent” while stressing that “we will keep driving the business and making decisions”.

Another key member of the investor group is WndrCo, the investment firm led by Jeffrey Katzenberg, the former Walt Disney Studios chairman and DreamWorks founder, and ex-Dropbox chief financial officer Sujay Jaswa. Fürste says “I don’t really have to explain” what expertise they can bring as Hyrox looks to grow its media footprint.

Up to now, media rights have accounted for a “super small” share of the company’s revenue, around 60 per cent of which comes from participation fees and spectator tickets. Marquee events are streamed on the Hyrox YouTube channel, while Atmosphere TV struck a deal last year to broadcast all Hyrox Majors and Regional Championships in more than 60,000 bars, restaurants, gyms and retail venues globally.

Traditional rights deals, though, have been few and far between. While revenue growth on that front isn’t necessarily being factored in to its business model, Fürste says it will be an “important part of the next stage for sure”, describing “the next big step” as improving the production of live races and other entertainment formats.

He believes that Hyrox is easier to broadcast compared to other endurance events like marathons and triathlons because it takes place within a condensed space, but says the focus is on “making it sexy so that people actually want to watch it”.

There appears to be some demand already in Germany, where Hyrox held its first race in 2017. Since this interview, the company has secured a broadcast deal with Axel Springer-owned Bild, which will air the remainder of the 2026/27 Elite Series after showing live coverage of the season-opener in Hamburg at the end of October.

If Fürste has his way, that deal won’t be the last.

“That development will be immense and we will see great development on the live broadcasting of Hyrox races,” he says. “I think it’s super exciting to watch. Obviously I’ve watched quite a few, and the production level has gone up quite consistently, and hopefully also with our new investors, we will invest a lot more into that space as well.

title: From views to subscriptions: SquashTV’s streaming growth story with Dailymotion
article_text:
Emerging sports do not necessarily lack content, fans or commercial potential. The challenge is that the digital sports ecosystem is fragmented: fans discover competitions through clips and social content, then watch live somewhere else.

For rights holders, the challenge is not simply making content discoverable. It is creating a destination where that interest becomes a direct, repeatable relationship with the sport.

That is where streaming platforms can play a decisive role.

A live tournament becomes a replay catalogue, supporting subscriptions, advertising and sponsorship. Streaming is therefore a critical growth factor for emerging sports: it enables rights value to compound over time.

SquashTV, the official streaming platform of the Professional Squash Association (PSA), offers a clear example of this model.

Initially launched in 2010, the service is a branded destination built around the PSA’s calendar, catalogue and international audience. For squash, it creates consistency between live tournaments and gives fans a reason to return.

Across the season, SquashTV generated more than 2.7 million video views and over 800,000 hours of streamed content. Those are significant figures for a specialist sport, but the more revealing metric is the platform’s target of 16 per cent year-on-year growth in subscribers and viewers.

While viewership shows that squash attracts attention, subscriber growth demonstrates that the platform is converting it into a more durable audience relationship.

For rights holders, the question becomes not only how many people watched an event, but what it contributes to the platform over time: new viewers, returning subscribers and catalogue value.

The platform therefore becomes more than a broadcast outlet: it increases frequency, retention and commercial value.

SquashTV ‘s development also illustrates the importance of control. A branded destination connects live matches, replays and archive content under one identity. The player is where fans experience that destination.

Dailymotion’s video technology, now part of its Edge offering, supports that experience through live and on-demand delivery and a player that can be tailored to the rights holder’s own brand. Edge lets media owners embed video in their own websites and applications and customise its appearance, helping keep the viewing experience consistent with their brand.

The model can evolve from free access and advertising to subscriptions, pay-per-view or hybrid, depending on audience maturity and viewing behaviour. But this model only works if the viewing experience supports repeat behaviour.

A fan may discover squash through a final, return for the next tournament and eventually subscribe. That progression depends on trust during important moments.

For SquashTV, dependable streaming infrastructure is part of the product. Dailymotion has partnered with the service for almost ten years as its audience and technical needs evolved.

At the PSA Squash Tour Finals in Paris, the platform delivered the event to subscribers in 1080p at 60 frames per second through a branded player, with real-time support and passes ranging from one to four days. The technology is crucial but intended to remain invisible: reliability, fluidity and playback quality are part of the reason viewers return.

For a fast-moving sport such as squash, 60-frame-per-second playback helps fans follow the ball and the pace of each rally. The player becomes part of the value of the service, particularly when viewers are paying to watch a live event.

The SquashTV and Dailymotion relationship is notable because it is not built around a single launch or one-off event.

Over ten years, the focus has evolved from live streaming, video on-demand (VOD) and global delivery to High Frame Rate, DVR and vertical video. Vertical formats responded to younger audiences who wanted to scroll through content on the rights holder’s own properties as naturally as on social platforms. More recently, AI-generated captions, translations and metadata have made the archive more accessible and discoverable in seconds, without manual work.

Edge’s player also supports adaptive streaming, which adjusts video quality to available bandwidth, and live rewind, which lets viewers pause and revisit moments during a live stream. Its wider capabilities include playlists, subtitles, chapters and playback analytics, giving media owners tools to make their catalogues easier to navigate and understand how audiences watch.

That long-term perspective matters because valuable streaming products are refined through repeated events and changing fan behaviour, not built in a single season.

The lesson for other sports is practical: infrastructure should do more than deliver the live event. It should make content discoverable, turn every match into replay and short-form inventory, support the right commercial model and give fans a reason to return.

For an emerging sport, that means building reach before extracting revenue, then moving from free discovery to registrations, hybrid models or subscriptions as loyalty grows. The infrastructure follows audience behaviour instead of imposing a fixed model.

SquashTV demonstrates why emerging sports do not need to wait for mainstream broadcast scale before building a media business. They need a passionate audience, a clear destination and a technology partner that can evolve with the way fans watch, discover and pay for content.

Streaming provides that foundation. It turns live rights into a branded destination, individual events into a growing catalogue and audience interest into measurable, compounding growth.

About the author: Kutay Vardar is director, inventory partnerships and video solutions at Dailymotion.

title: WXV Global Series 2026 review: England's Red Roses
article_text:
England had a mixed bag of results in the WXV Global Series but the team will have learned more from this campaign than it has since their Rugby World Cup final loss in 2022 and it has come at the perfect time.

The Red Roses, who won their eighth consecutive Guinness Women’s Six Nations title in May, did come away with three wins, a draw and two losses but it was those latter results that garnered most attention.

England were unable to beat Canada across three matches with two defeats and a draw with their Women’s Rugby World Cup 2025 final opponents, who were absolutely on the money when coming up against their rivals.

Kévin Rouet’s side had been open about putting everything into wanting to beat England and they achieved that objective but inadvertently gave England their biggest learnings in four years.

That’s because England had not lost since that final in 2022. The head coach John Mitchell said he will learn more from the losses than he had the wins and Abi Burton told RugbyPass that weak elements of a team’s game are magnified after a loss, meaning they will look more in depth at where they can get better and grow. This was the best time for the losses to come too with no trophy on the line.

While there were elements all round to improve for England, there were two particular areas in the games in Ottawa and Toronto where Canada gained huge momentum: Scrappy attack and a malfunctioning lineout. Knock-ons and loose passes accounted for multiple opportunities going begging and Canada had also worked out England’s attacking plans A and B. They wrapped Ellie Kildunne up with multiple tacklers rendering the star full-back out of the game and their high press defence and slowing the ball down at the breakdown made it difficult for England to get front foot ball.

It wasn’t all bad for England. They will know and take heart that they were not blown away by Canada. The first loss was by three points and the second by nine points. Each match was a close encounter and made for thrilling viewing for those watching. That is the other benefit of teams catching the Red Roses up, not only are fans seeing new game winners but they are able to be enthralled by classic Test matches.

WXV Global Series was not all full of losses for England either with wins over Australia, New Zealand and the USA. After the series of matches they are also still world No.1s but not everything has remained the same, there was a shake up in the line-up over the last two matches.

Kildunne’s containment and a drop in form saw her benched with Emma Sing starting at full-back with a change at wing too with Mia Venner starting the final two matches with Claudia Moloney-MacDonald first dropped and then Jess Breach. Sing had solid performances but Venner really marked out a place for herself with impressive outings on both occasions.

There is a lot of time between now and England’s next match at the start of the 2027 Women’s Six Nations in April and so supporters will have to wait to see if they have claimed those starting shirts in the long term. That won’t just depend on the campaign just gone of course, with the players needing to retain form throughout the JAECOO Premiership Women’s Rugby season.

There were also players who maintained great form for England across all six WXV Global Series games, namely Bryony Field, Maddie Feaunati, Zoe Harrison and the captain Meg Jones. Others also had good performances but those four were standouts.

Field in particular was impressive, winning her first cap against Australia in September and claiming a starting shirt for the close clash against the Black Ferns before playing a role in all of the other matches. She will cause Mitchell some selection headaches at hooker, especially now Lark Atkin-Davies is back in the mix after returning to the pitch following the birth of her daughter, Olive.

England ended their WXV Global Series campaign with a victory over the USA so they will be left with a winning feeling before taking to the pitch again. They will also be favourites to win their ninth Women’s Six Nations in a row with the only realistic challengers to the title being France, whose form took a nosedive in October.

While they were missing many of their main stars like Pauline Bourdon Sansus and Manae Feleu for their series in New Zealand, they were beaten repeatedly over three Tests by the Black Ferns. New Zealand won the three games by an aggregate score of 148-31, with the first game 81-12, which doesn’t paint a promising title-winning picture for next year. But they will play England at Allianz Stadium which is where they have come close to beating England in recent years.

So England’s winning domination has been slightly halted this WXV Global Series with their 41-game unbeaten record over. But they have already begun another winning era and fans will have to watch this space for how long that will continue with the knowledge that England will not play Canada or New Zealand until 2028 because of the inaugural women’s British & Irish Lions tour in 2027.

title: Mady Sow Keeps Europe's Medal Hopes Alive in Dakar
article_text:
France's Mady Sow is the last European player standing at the Youth Olympic Games 2026, having secured his place in the men's singles quarterfinals after three days of group-stage action in Dakar, Senegal.

With 18 European players competing across men's and women's singles, a lot of European talents have been in action. However, with only the winner of each group progressing to the knockout stage, the competition has proven challenging for Europe's young talents.

One player who has lived up to expectations is top seed Mady Sow. The 16-year-old Frenchman, who claimed bronze at last month's World Junior Championships, has successfully made his way through Group A and remains in contention for a Youth Olympic medal.

Sow now faces sixth seed Rithik Rasamsetti of the USA in Wednesday's quarterfinals, with a place in the semifinals on the line.

Although Sow is the only European to progress, several others have delivered promising performances throughout the group stage.

Among them was Great Britain's Rajvi Parab, who came particularly close to reaching the women's singles quarterfinals.

Parab made an impressive start to her campaign, winning her opening two matches against Ukraine's Varvara Poperezhai and Uganda's Ramiah Bukenya. However, she ultimately missed out on the top spot in Group C and a place in the knockout stage, after a 21-19 19-21 15-21 loss to USA's Micah Henares Cruz.

For now, all European eyes turn to Mady Sow as he looks to keep his medal dreams alive and take another step towards Youth Olympic glory in Dakar.

He will be playing quarterfinals this morning, and if he advances semifinals will be played in the afternoon today.

article_text:
Riyan Malhan of United Arab Emirates will taken on Punnatat Prempunpong of Thailand in the quarterfinals of the Youth Olympic Games in Dakar.

In their final group matches yesterday, Malhan beat Lucas Lee (Malaysia), while Prempunpong overcame Singapore’s Ng Zhen Hong Zack, both in straight games.

Malhan has made waves over the last two seasons; earlier this year he was the first player from UAE to win a Badminton Asia tournament, after he won the BAC U17 title in Chengdu this year.

His quarterfinal opponent, Prempunpong, has been marked as one of the talents to watch in Thailand. Training at Bangthongyord Club, Prempungpong was won praise from his senior compatriot Kunlavut Vitidsarn. The Thai had fallen in a close quarterfinal at the World Juniors; his best result of the season was a runner-up place at the Malaysia Junior International Challenge in July.

In women’s singles, Hong Kong China’s Ip Sum Yau will have an opportunity to avenge her loss at the recent BWF World Junior Championships 2026 when she takes on Zhang Yi Xin in the quarterfinals.

The two clashed at the semifinal stage in Cairo, with Zhang winning a hard-fought three-game battle; she would go on to claim the gold the next day beating Japan’s Saki Matsumoto.

Zhang, who faintly resembles the now-retired (and former YOG champion) He Bing Jiao, has played only two tournaments this year before arriving at the YOG. She made the final of the Badminton Asia (BAC) Junior Championships, where she was beaten by compatriot Yin Yi Qing. Interestingly, she played just one tournament last year – the BAC U17, while in 2023, her only appearance was at the BAC Junior Championships in doubles.

Ip was the first singles medalist for Hong Kong China at the World Juniors. She’s had a prolific season, winning a senior tournament (Latvia International), and at the junior level, the Jaya Raya Junior International, Yonex 3 Borders, Valamar Junior Open, Cyprus Junior, and Bulgarian Junior International.

The lineup does feature several accomplished junior stars. Sow is already reckoned to be France’s next big talent, and the European Junior champion was voted Badminton Europe Player of the Year earlier this year.

Tanvi Patri is regarded as one of India’s brightest young talents, having made her presence felt even at senior tournaments. Her results include two titles (BAC U17 and Pontianak International Challenge) and three runner-up places (Austrian Open, Latvia International, Singapore International).

Patri will expect a tough quarterfinal, for her opponent Kakanik Kungkaew has had an impressive season too, with titles at the Philippines Junior, Malaysia Junior and Pathumthanee Junior International tournaments.

Following the quarterfinals, the semifinals too will be played today (Wednesday 4 November).

title: Indian marketers bet big on sports sponsorship as audience gateway
article_text:
Nielsen’s 2026 Annual Marketing Report shows Indian marketers leading six markets in planned spending increases on sponsorship and event media. The survey also finds India ahead on viewing sports sponsorship as a way to test new audiences, even as measurement of returns remains weak.

Indian brands are preparing to lean harder into live experiences, sports properties and creator-led marketing, even as many still struggle to track whether those bets pay off. Nielsen’s 2026 Annual Marketing Report, cited by Business Standard, suggests India is emerging as the most aggressive market among six surveyed when it comes to sponsorship and event media spending plans.India expect to raise spending on sponsorship and event media over the next 12 to 24 months. That is the highest share among the six markets studied and points to a broader shift in how brands are thinking about reach, relevance and audience discovery. The survey covered 1,200 marketers in India, the US, the UK, Italy, France and Germany, with 200 respondents from each market.Live events are moving up the marketing agendaNielsen data is not just higher spending intent, but where that money is likely to go. The company’s survey measured sponsorship and event media as a wider category that includes sporting as well as cultural events, so the findings reflect a broader appetite for live audience engagement rather than only sports-specific deals. Even so, sports remains central to the conversation because of its scale, fan loyalty and ability to deliver repeated exposure across platforms.India sees sports as a testing groundsports sponsorship itself. A majority of respondents in India, 61 per cent, said sports sponsorship serves as a way to test new audiences and markets.
